headline: NASA Releases Over 800GB of Artemis II Science Data Online

body.text: NASA has made a massive archive from the Artemis II mission publicly available on its new "Artemis II: Sights & Sounds of Science" website. The collection totals more than 800 gigabytes of raw data, including over 11,000 photos and videos captured during the flight.

In addition to visual media, the archive contains more than 8.5 hours of audio recordings, many of which feature annotations by the crew members themselves. The material provides scientists and the public with unprecedented insight into the mission’s operations and observations.

The release is part of NASA’s effort to increase transparency and support ongoing research related to lunar exploration. Users can download the files directly from the site for analysis or educational purposes.
Why It Matters
The open access to Artemis II data helps researchers and educators in the US and Europe advance lunar science and technology development.

key_points: NASA posted over 800GB of Artemis II data, images, and audio on a dedicated website.

source_summary: The boat was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen with 305 people on board, when it capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night.

body.text: A boat traveling from Djibouti to Yemen capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night, according to the United Nations. The vessel was carrying 305 people when it overturned, resulting in 139 confirmed deaths.

Rescue teams recovered bodies and pulled survivors from the water, but many passengers remain unaccounted for. The incident underscores the perilous conditions faced by migrants and refugees attempting the crossing between the Horn of Africa and the Arabian Peninsula.

The UN has called for urgent attention to the safety of such sea journeys, noting that the loss of life could have been higher if not for the swift response of local authorities and international aid workers.
Why It Matters
The disaster illustrates the ongoing humanitarian risks on migration routes that link Africa and the Middle East, a concern for international aid and security agencies.
